previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, HIV, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for MRSA bacteremia originating from her left femoral dialysis catheter. She presented with malaise, weakness, and catheter site pain. The infected catheter was removed, and a temporary line was placed. A stent was successfully inserted to treat underlying IVC stenosis. She experienced transient hyperkalemia requiring urgent dialysis but stabilized. Blood cultures cleared, and she completed a line holiday before receiving a new right femoral tunneled dialysis catheter. Her antibiotics were continued, warfarin was adjusted, and HIV medication adherence was addressed. She was discharged to extended care to complete her six-week vancomycin course with plans for ongoing support.
problems: Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter
Herpes zoster with other nervous system complications

HISTORY:  ___ female with hypotension, on dialysis.  Evaluation for
pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to radiograph of the chest from ___.

FINDINGS:  A single semi-upright AP view of the chest demonstrates interval
placement of a large-bore dialysis catheter through an inferior approach,
which terminates in the right atrium.  Convex bulging of the right mediastinal
contour is slightly more conspicuous than on the prior study.  The lungs are
well inflated and clear bilaterally with no evidence of pneumothorax, pleural
effusion, pulmonary edema, or focal consolidation concerning for pneumonia. 
Right axillary surgical clips are again noted.

IMPRESSION:  Thickening and convex bulging of the right mediastinal contour is
more prominent than on the prior study. Please correlate with dedicated PA and
lateral CXR.  No evidence of pneumonia. Inferior approach hemodialysis
catheter terminates in the right atrium.

EXAMINATION:  BILAT LOWER EXT VEINS

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with recent right HD line placement who
presents with right thigh pain  // ? evidence of DVT

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale, color, and spectral Doppler evaluation was performed
on the bilateral lower extremity veins.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

Visualization of the right common femoral vein is noted to be somewhat limited
due to an intravenous line. There is normal compressibility, flow and
augmentation of bilateral common femoral, femoral, and popliteal veins. Normal
color flow and compressibility are demonstrated in the posterior tibial and
peroneal veins.

There is normal respiratory variation in the common femoral veins bilaterally.

No evidence of medial popliteal fossa (___) cyst.

IMPRESSION:
